scenes.vo: Attackers aren't stopping at the network anymore. They're going after the controllers themselves.
If your PLCs or relays were changed tonight, would anyone notice?
Without a golden baseline, a malicious change looks like routine engineering.

text.headline: A malicious change looks like *routine engineering.*

scenes.vo: Each vendor ships its own proprietary software, often thousands of dollars a license, designed for engineering, not security.
There's a better way to look at the control layer.

text.line1: There's a better way to see

scenes.vo: PEAT. The Process Extraction and Analysis Tool, developed at Sandia National Laboratories.
First, it discovers and identifies the devices on your network.

text.title: Discover and *identify* devices
text.sub: Network discovery with vendor and model verification.

scenes.vo: Next, it collects the logic, configuration, logs, and firmware from each one.

text.title: Collect *logic, config, logs & firmware*
text.sub: Over Ethernet or serial, straight from the device.

scenes.vo: Then it decodes vendor formats into a single, consistent data model.

text.title: Decode into *one data model*
text.sub: Vendor-specific formats become consistent, structured JSON.

scenes.vo: Diff every pull against your golden config, and any unapproved change stands out. Elastic and Splunk work out of the box.

text.title: Catch *every change*
text.sub: Diff against your golden config. Elastic & Splunk built in.

scenes.vo: It's built for OT, safety first. Devices are verified before anything is collected, one at a time, and you control exactly what gets pulled.
It supports PLCs, protection relays, RTUs, and more, from over ten vendors.

text.headline: Field devices from *10+ vendors*
text.footer: 25+ device families · 13 protocols · project files & disk images

scenes.vo: Now you can see your controllers clearly, and know what they're actually doing.
PEAT runs on Linux, Windows, macOS, or Docker. Once it's downloaded, it works fully offline, so your configurations never touch the cloud.
It's also a Python library, so you can script PEAT into your own workflows.

text.title: A *Python library*, too
text.sub: Script PEAT into your own workflows and tooling.

scenes.vo: No license fees. PEAT is free, open source, and GPL licensed.
Security is what you inspect, not what you expect. Get PEAT on GitHub today.
